kurz: Anthropic heads for the Nasdaq this week under the ticker ANT
American MBA applications are slumping as demand drifts towards Europe and Asia
Goldman Sachs sets out a cooler 2027: slower earnings growth and a trimmed gold forecast

meldungen.titel: Anthropic heads for the Nasdaq this week under the ticker ANT
meldungen.text:
The listing that much of the AI industry has been waiting for is now days away. According to an amended S-1 filed on 10 November, Anthropic intends to float on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT", offering 825 million Class A shares at an indicative $70 to $78 apiece. Underwriters hold an option on a further 123.75 million shares. IPO calendars pencil in the first day of trading for Thursday, 19 November; Trending Topics likewise lists the debut among next week's market events.

The headline valuation varies with the source. Renaissance Capital speaks of a market capitalisation of roughly $1.2 trillion, other outlets of $1.3 to $1.4 trillion, with gross proceeds of up to about $64 billion. Alongside the offering, a separate private placement of some $26 billion in a different share class is reported to be priced at the IPO price. Reports from September had pointed to an October debut, so the timetable has already slipped once.

The benchmark everyone is watching is SpaceX, whose record Nasdaq listing reportedly closed its first day about 20 per cent above its $135 issue price. Whether Anthropic can repeat that depends on a market that has turned jittery: Nvidia has just lost its founder, Bitcoin is sliding and a December rate rise by the Federal Reserve is now all but priced in. The price range may still change before trading starts.
meldungen.quelle: Renaissance Capital, The Next Web, Trending Topics

meldungen.titel: Jensen Huang is gone, and Nvidia must learn to function without the man it was built around
meldungen.text:
The most consequential week of the AI boom so far has ended with Nvidia's co-founder out of the building. Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive after several extramarital affairs became public, among them a relationship with Alice Huang, a woman US investigators suspect of being a Chinese agent, and two with employees. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has taken over on an interim basis. Huang has been summoned to a hearing before Congress.

The affairs grab the headlines, but the real question is about chips. Alice Huang, a former presenter on Chinese state television who later moved into finance and then cloud infrastructure, took a majority stake in the Singapore "neocloud" Megaspeed International in 2023. Within months Megaspeed became an official Nvidia Cloud Partner with preferential access to AI chips. According to CBS News, Megaspeed and its Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix bought Nvidia hardware worth around $4.8 billion over three years, and investigators believe Alice Huang gained access to some 240,000 chips whose export to China was banned. Whether the processors were installed in Malaysia and rented remotely to Chinese firms, or smuggled into China outright, remains unclear. Financial links to Alibaba can be traced through a web of companies. The Justice Department and the FBI are investigating possible export control violations; US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday no conclusion had yet been reached on whether she was a spy. If Huang is shown to have been complicit, he could face prison.

The commercial stakes are vast. Nvidia was the first company worth $5 trillion and on its own accounts for about 6 per cent of the S&P 500. Huang, 63, once said he would rather die on the job and made no succession plans; around 60 people reported directly to him. "Jensen is Nvidia, and Nvidia is Jensen," the analyst Jon Peddie told The Verge. His career was a string of company-or-bust wagers, from the Riva 128 graphics card, shipped with a month of payroll left, to CUDA, a feature nobody had asked for that raised the cost of every GeForce card by half and became the foundation of today's AI computing.

Speaking on the Trending Topics podcast, Clemens Wasner, chair of AI Austria, called it the deepest rupture since the boom began, comparable to Steve Jobs leaving Apple in the 1980s. Up to 22 per cent of Nvidia's revenue reportedly ran through Singapore. An interim chief with less appetite for so-called circular deals could also slow Nvidia's investments in OpenAI, Anthropic, neoclouds and European start-ups. The share price, meanwhile, now sits below its level of a year ago despite sharply higher revenue and profit.

meldungen.titel: American MBA applications are slumping as demand drifts towards Europe and Asia
meldungen.text:
Georgetown's McDonough School of Business has become the latest emblem of a sharp downturn in American business school demand. The student paper The Hoya reports that applications to its full-time MBA fell by nearly a quarter this cycle; figures compiled by Bloomberg from school data put the drop at 22 per cent. Either way, it ends two consecutive years of strong growth.

Georgetown is no outlier. The Graduate Management Admission Council's 2026 application survey, published on 27 October, found applications to full-time MBA programmes down 27 per cent, and Poets&Quants summarised the broader picture as US business school applications plunging by around a quarter while global demand shifts to Europe and Asia.

For European schools, that shift cuts both ways: more applications mean healthier pipelines and, potentially, stiffer competition for places and scholarships in the coming rounds.

meldungen.titel: Goldman Sachs sets out a cooler 2027: slower earnings growth and a trimmed gold forecast
meldungen.text:
Goldman Sachs has published its forecasts for 2027, and the tone is one of deceleration rather than alarm. The bank expects only a modest rise in European equities next year. Its strategists argue that corporate earnings growth in 2026 was exceptional, flattered by AI investment and higher energy prices, and will slow in 2027 while remaining supportive of share prices. Earlier this autumn the bank had put its 12-month target for the STOXX Europe 600 at 695 points, roughly 7 per cent above the level at the time; Bloomberg Intelligence consensus expects European profits to rise 9 per cent in 2027 after about 15 per cent this year.

Goldman is markedly more upbeat on Asia excluding Japan, where it forecasts a total return of 19 per cent in 2027. At the same time it trimmed its 2027 gold forecast, to $4,650 per troy ounce according to German financial press reports. The bank's own share price was the standout in the Dow Jones last week, contributing some 300 index points on its own.

meldungen.titel: Thousands of apps built with Lovable left their databases open to strangers
meldungen.text:
The vibe coding boom has produced its most sobering audit yet. The German security firm Crissy Field, working with the business daily Handelsblatt, found that thousands of web apps built with the AI platform Lovable let anyone read their databases without logging in. Exposed records include passport numbers, payment details and private chat messages.

Using the open web archive Common Crawl, the researchers identified 159,041 Lovable projects online between December 2025 and September 2026. Of these, 34,545 used the database service Supabase, and 24,664 sent database records to the browser on loading. With further read-only requests using the very API key each page already transmits, the team found tables containing email addresses on 7,403 sites, about 30 per cent of those examined in depth. Crissy Field stresses this is not a confirmed leak rate, since some addresses are public contacts or test data.

The examples are stark: more than 1,000 records with passport numbers from one service provider; a German lifestyle forum exposing over 80,000 profiles and more than 200,000 chat messages; event organisers and restaurants revealing tens of thousands of orders with addresses, payment information and valid ticket codes; and a property manager leaking AI-generated summaries of internal emails about tenants. In one case 280,000 customer emails were accessible. Whether any data was misused could not be established.

No break-in was required. Supabase's browser key is public by design; the data is protected only by Row Level Security rules inside the database, and where those are missing or lax, anyone can read the tables. Because Lovable apps follow recurring patterns, a single misconfiguration can be scanned for across thousands of sites. Lovable calls it a known, industry-wide Supabase configuration issue and points to its security scan and AI reviewer, introduced after a similar flaw (CVE-2025-48757) surfaced in 2025. Yet the platform markets itself to non-experts while its terms place security responsibility on customers. The Stockholm company was last valued at $13.3 billion, with $400 million in annual recurring revenue this spring.

meldungen.titel: LangChain raises $300 million, more than doubling its valuation to $3 billion in a year
meldungen.text:
Whoever builds AI agents needs someone to keep watch over them, and that proposition has just earned LangChain a multibillion-dollar price tag. The US start-up closed a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation, led by existing investor CapitalG, Alphabet's growth fund. New backers include Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC, DFJ Growth and Salesforce Ventures. A year ago LangChain raised $125 million at $1.25 billion.

The company made its name with the open-source framework of the same name, which connects language models to data and tools. Chief executive Harrison Chase has since built a commercial business around LangSmith, a platform for running, improving and governing agents regardless of the framework or model behind them. It covers runtime (cloud or self-hosted, or fully managed), improvement (observability, evaluation, an in-house agent that hunts for errors and proposes fixes, and fine-tuning from agent logs) and governance (gateways that control which models and tools agents may use, with budgets and fallbacks).

More than 7,000 organisations use LangSmith, from Harvey and Rippling to Nvidia, Toyota and Salesforce; at Workday the time to deploy a new agent reportedly fell from five months to under a day. Competition is dense, from Arize, Braintrust and Langfuse (bought by ClickHouse in January) to the model makers' own toolkits from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Developers have long grumbled that LangChain's layers of abstraction overcomplicate simple tasks. New features are due to be unveiled on Friday.

meldungen.titel: Bitcoin slides to $65,000 as a billion dollars of leveraged bets are wiped out
meldungen.text:
The weekend has brought crypto investors no respite. Bitcoin fell to about $65,000 on Saturday afternoon, its lowest since the summer, down more than 5 per cent in 24 hours and almost 14 per cent on the week. Having broken below $69,000 on Friday, it has also pierced its 200-week moving average of around $68,000, a level long-term holders watch closely. The largest cryptocurrency now trades almost 49 per cent below its record of roughly $126,000 from October 2025.

Altcoins are faring worse. Solana, Cardano and Hyperliquid each lost close to 10 per cent in a day, XRP slipped below $1 and Ether below $1,850; the whole market shed over 7 per cent to about $2.22 trillion. According to CoinGlass, positions worth $1.01 billion were forcibly liquidated within 24 hours, 93 per cent of them bets on rising prices, affecting more than 195,000 traders. US Bitcoin ETFs saw $1.07 billion of outflows in the week to Friday, the most since late June, and BlackRock's IBIT has bled money for 11 straight trading days.

The main driver is fear of tighter money. US core inflation rose 0.3 per cent in October, Fed governor Christopher Waller has backed a December rate rise of at least a quarter point, and futures now treat a hike as near certain. The dollar index is above 103, its highest since April 2025, which hurts an asset that pays no yield. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index has sunk to 13, deep in "extreme fear".

Bulls note that Bitcoin is technically oversold, with a relative strength index near 25, and that ETFs still hold about $55 billion of net inflows since launch. Bears point to support at $64,700, then $58,600, and some warn of $50,000. The coming week brings fresh ETF data on Monday, the Fed's October minutes on Wednesday and Anthropic's Nasdaq debut.

meldungen.titel: The case against "proteinmaxxing" gains ground, though the evidence remains contested
meldungen.text:
Science magazine scinexx this weekend joined a growing chorus questioning the high-protein trend, reporting on research suggesting that a lower-protein diet may slow ageing. The debate has been fuelled by a review from researchers at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, who evaluated more than 300 studies and concluded that restricting protein can slow ageing processes.

The picture is far from settled. Mouse experiments cited in the coverage found that moderate protein intake produced the healthiest metabolism, while very low-protein diets caused mild fatty liver in middle-aged animals. A study in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, by contrast, found a high-protein, lower-calorie diet beneficial for older adults, and European bodies such as the German Nutrition Society (DGE) have kept their existing recommendations unchanged. Euronews noted that a low-protein diet is not suitable for everyone.
